description: Build the core memory service layer with SQLite persistence, BM25 text search, memory consolidation, and decay - inspired by agentmemory's architecture but implemented as a self-contained Python module within the existing Flask backend.
steps: Step 1: Add SQLite dependency to backend/pyproject.toml (sqlite3 is stdlib, but add 'rank-bm25' for BM25 search). Also add 'numpy' as a lightweight dependency for similarity computations.

Step 2: Create backend/app/models/memory.py with SQLAlchemy-free dataclasses for memory entities: MemoryEntry (id, content, summary, memory_type enum [observation/episodic/semantic/procedural], importance float 0-1, access_count, created_at, last_accessed, session_id, tags list, metadata dict), Session (id, idea_text, summary, started_at, ended_at, status), and MemorySearchResult (entry, relevance_score).

Step 3: Create backend/app/services/memory_store.py - SQLite-backed storage layer. Singleton pattern matching TaskManager. Methods: init_db() creates tables (memories, sessions), save_memory(entry), get_memory(id), search_memories(query, limit, memory_type_filter), list_sessions(limit, offset), get_session(id), save_session(session), delete_memory(id), update_access(id). Use context managers for connections. DB file at configurable path (default: backend/data/memory.sqlite).

Step 4: Create backend/app/services/memory_search.py - BM25 search engine class. Methods: index_memories(memories list), search(query, top_k=5) returns ranked MemorySearchResult list. Tokenizes content using simple whitespace + lowercasing. Rebuilds index on each search call (or caches with invalidation flag).

Step 5: Create backend/app/services/memory_service.py - High-level memory service orchestrating store + search. Singleton like TaskManager. Methods: remember(content, memory_type, importance, session_id, tags, metadata) -> MemoryEntry, recall(query, limit=5, memory_type_filter=None) -> list[MemorySearchResult], forget(memory_id) -> bool, get_session_history(limit=10) -> list[Session], start_session(idea_text) -> Session, end_session(session_id, summary) -> Session, consolidate() runs decay and consolidation logic, inject_context(query) -> str returns formatted context string for LLM injection.

Step 6: Implement memory decay in memory_service.py: memories lose importance over time (Ebbinghaus-inspired curve), memories accessed frequently get boosted, memories below threshold (0.1) are auto-deleted. Run consolidate() periodically or on session end.

Step 7: Implement context injection in memory_service.py: inject_context(query) searches memories, formats top results as a context block string suitable for prepending to LLM system prompts. Includes session summaries and relevant past observations.
Step 8: Add MEMORY_DB_PATH config to backend/app/config.py (default: 'data/memory.sqlite' relative to backend dir). Add MEMORY_ENABLED flag (default: true).

Step 9: Create backend/tests/test_memory_service.py with tests for: save/retrieve memories, BM25 search finds relevant results, memory decay reduces importance, session lifecycle (start/end), context injection formats properly. Use temporary SQLite db (in-memory or tempfile).
acceptance_criteria: MemoryService can store and retrieve memories with SQLite persistence
BM25 search returns relevant memories ranked by relevance when queried
Memory decay reduces importance of old/unused memories over time
Session lifecycle (start, end with summary) works correctly
inject_context() returns a formatted string with relevant past context
All new tests pass with pytest
